title: Basic Memory: markdown files as agent memory over MCP
by: Basic Machines' open-source (AGPL) Python server. Read: the README and docs/ai-assistant-guide-extended.md (the 1.0 MCP tool guide), via raw.githubusercontent.com.
summary: Basic Memory keeps knowledge as plain Markdown files that people and agents both edit, with a local SQLite index for search. Each file is an entity with frontmatter, observations ('- [category] fact') and relations ('- relates_to [[Other]]'). Agents work through a small, named set of MCP tools, and writes are guarded by checksums and an explicit overwrite flag.
ideas: A fixed tool set: bm_write, bm_read, bm_edit, bm_move, bm_delete, bm_search, bm_list, bm_find, bm_context, bm_project, bm_schema and bm_man, each tagged read-only, destructive or idempotent.
bm_write creates and refuses to replace an existing note unless overwrite=True; a full replace must pass the expected_checksum from the read.
bm_edit has named commands (append, prepend, find_replace, replace_section, insert_before_section, insert_after_section, set_metadata), and expected_replacements must match the real count.
Optimistic concurrency: on a revision conflict the agent must re-read and reconcile before retrying.
bm_schema validate, infer and diff check notes against a type's structure and find drift; inference proposes and never rewrites.
Errors are explicit codes (NOT_FOUND, ALREADY_EXISTS, INVALID_ARGUMENTS), and an empty search is not a failed search.
The files are the truth and the index is rebuilt from them; a doctor command checks file and index agree.
Move to an archive instead of deleting when provenance matters, and link related notes before deleting a source.

took.idea: Create refuses to overwrite; a replace carries the hash of the version it read
Named edit operations instead of free file writes
schema validate and diff as a standing check for drift
Tag each verb read-only or destructive so agents and permissions can tell
Files are the truth, every index is derived and rebuildable
